$comment: shadcn/ui as a GUML theme. The default one.
Class strings and tokens taken from shadcn/ui's own `registry/new-york-v4/ui/*.tsx` — the button's
variant set, the input's border and ring treatment, the badge's tone set, the table's cell metrics.
The token names are shadcn's exactly: `--background`/`--foreground` pairs, `--primary`,
`--secondary`, `--muted`, `--accent`, `--destructive`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--card`,
`--popover`, `--sidebar`, `--radius`. So a host that already runs shadcn drops this in and its own
palette applies with no further work: the variables are the interface.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CARRIED, because a class table cannot:
* Radix behaviour. shadcn's dialog traps focus, its select is a listbox with keyboard navigation,
its tooltip positions itself. Those are components, not classes. GUML's `modal`, `select` and
`drawer` get shadcn's *appearance* and the compiler's own semantics — a real `<select>`, a
`<template>` in the no-JavaScript build. A host that wants Radix behaviour points a registry
package at its own components with `element`/`import`; that is what `packages/guml-widgets`
demonstrates.
* `data-[state=...]` and `aria-invalid:` variants. They key off attributes Radix sets, and this
compiler does not emit them, so a rule for them would be dead.
* `[&_svg]` descendant selectors. GUML has no icon primitive yet, so there is nothing to select.
Every class here has a rule in `shadcn.css`, enforced by
`every_class_the_builtin_theme_emits_has_a_rule_in_its_stylesheet`. That is not decoration: the
static-HTML backend has no build step, so it inlines this stylesheet, and a class with no rule is a
silently unstyled no-JavaScript page.
